{"id":"PKIX-z47k","title":"pkix-ct: is Apple's CT log list signed, and how?","description":"## What

pkix-ct documents Apple and browser-specific log lists as alternative sources, ingested by constructing CtLog values and calling CtLogList::insert. PKIX-eits added signature verification for Google's list; Apple's was out of scope there and was not investigated.

## Questions

1. Does Apple publish a detached signature over its log list, and with what key and algorithm? Google publishes log_list.json, log_list.sig and log_list_pubkey.pem; Apple's distribution may differ in shape or may rely on HTTPS alone.
2. If it is signed, does the existing from_google_log_list_json_verified shape generalise, or does Apple's schema differ enough to need its own parser? The schemas are known to differ.
3. If it is not signed, say so in the crate docs. A consumer pinning an unsigned list should know that the HTTPS fetch is the only thing authenticating it.

## Why it is P4

Nobody in this workspace pins Apple's list today, and the Google path is now verified. This matters when a consumer wants Apple's log-inclusion policy rather than Google's -- which is a real reason to choose it, since the two programs admit logs on different terms, and a consumer should be choosing that deliberately rather than by whichever list they found first.

## Acceptance

[ ] Apple's list distribution documented: signed or not, and how if so
[ ] If signed, either verified by the same shape or a reason recorded for why it needs its own

{"notes":"ANSWERED 2026-11-24, by fetching. Apple's CT log list is NOT SIGNED. Its authenticity rests entirely on HTTPS to valid.apple.com.

## What Apple publishes

  https://valid.apple.com/ct/log_list/current_log_list.json   200, ~154 KB, 17 operators

## What Apple does not publish

No detached signature at any plausible path:

  current_log_list.json.sig   404
  log_list.sig                404
  current_log_list.sig        404
  log_list_pubkey.pem         404

And no signature inside the document. Its top-level keys are exactly: $schema, assetVersion, assetVersionV2, operators, version. Nothing signature-shaped.

Contrast Google, which publishes all three artifacts and whose list is therefore cryptographically verifiable (see the CT log-list signature bead):

  log_list.json  +  log_list.sig  +  log_list_pubkey.pem

## Consequence for the per-program anchor crate family

This was raised as a condition on admitting a pkix-ct-google crate: that it be one of a family rather than Google privileged. The family cannot be symmetric, and not because of any choice on our side.

- Google: signed, so the crate ships a KEY and the list is verified at fetch time. The key rotates rarely, the list churns weekly, and a drift check against the published list is meaningful.
- Apple: unsigned, so there is no key to ship. The only options are pinning a snapshot of the 154 KB list, which goes stale in weeks and cannot be verified on refresh, or trusting HTTPS. Pinning a snapshot is the shape already rejected for Google's list on cadence grounds, and it is strictly worse here because no signature exists to validate a refresh against.

So a pkix-ct-apple in the same shape is not possible. A consumer choosing Apple's log program gets HTTPS-only authenticity, full stop.

## What should happen regardless of the crate decision

pkix-ct's documentation currently lists Apple and browser-specific lists as alternative sources, ingested via CtLogList::insert, without saying anything about their authenticity. Now that from_google_log_list_json_verified exists, a reader can reasonably infer that the alternatives are similarly verifiable. They are not. The crate should say which alternative sources are authenticated and which are not.

## Worth checking before concluding Apple has no mechanism

Apple may authenticate the list through a channel not visible at these URLs -- an OS-level signed asset bundle, or distribution inside a signed system update rather than over plain HTTPS. That would authenticate it for Apple's own platforms while leaving a third-party fetcher with HTTPS only, which is a different claim from "unsigned" and worth stating precisely if anyone pins it. Not investigated.

## Acceptance

[x] Apple's list distribution documented: NOT signed, HTTPS-only at the published URL
[x] Reason recorded for why it cannot use the same shape as the Google path
[ ] pkix-ct docs state which alternative log-list sources are authenticated and which are not"}

ANSWERED and documented. Apple's CT log list is NOT signed: no detached signature at any plausible path (current_log_list.json.sig, log_list.sig, current_log_list.sig, log_list_pubkey.pem all 404) and no signature field in the document, whose top-level keys are exactly $schema, assetVersion, assetVersionV2, operators, version.

pkix-ct's module documentation now states which alternative log-list sources are authenticated and which are not, closing the third acceptance item. Previously it listed Apple beside Google as an alternative source without distinguishing them, which -- once a verified constructor existed for Google's list -- invited the inference that the alternatives were comparably authenticated.

Not investigated, and worth stating as a limit: Apple may authenticate the list through a channel not visible at those URLs, such as a signed OS asset bundle or distribution inside a signed system update. That would authenticate it for Apple's own platforms while still leaving a third-party fetcher with HTTPS only, which is a different claim from 'unsigned' and would be worth stating precisely if anyone pins it.
